initiative.title: Agent inbox: notes to AI, annotations, and replies
initiative.summary: Let Byron leave requests and text annotations on notes for polling MCP agents, let agents annotate and reply, and show the whole back-and-forth in one central inbox.
initiative.next_action: Byron: review stack #300-#304 and layer 5, merge, deploy, then run the live scheduled-task check in app/docs/agent-inbox.md.

sources.anchor: Rules: ownership, metadata is open, deleting stays with the user
model ChatThread / ChatMessage (per-note in-app LLM sidebar)
Note storage (blocks): every block carries a stable id
scheduled tasks reach connected apps (vendor blog, unverified with OpenAI docs)

claims.statement: Byron wants an asynchronous channel to MCP agents that poll on a schedule: he leaves work, they pick it up later.
Requests are created while interacting with notes and other content in the app, not in a separate form.
A quick 'note to AI' control on a note adds a top-level request (research, follow up, expand).
Selected text can be annotated; it shows as a colored highlight with the annotation in a side rail; agents can read and act on it.
Agents can add their own annotations to notes through MCP.
One central place shows the inbox, agent feedback, and the back-and-forth, so Byron never has to open each note to check.
'Every N hours' polling is the expected agent behavior; the cadence is an example, not a requirement.
Agents may not change the body of notes Byron wrote; 'expand this content' requests collide with that rule.
Research comments already follow a 'user leaves, agent resolves with a note' pattern that this feature could generalize.
Each request is a task with a status (open, in progress, done) and a reply thread both sides can add to.
For edits to Byron's own notes, the agent proposes a change and Byron accepts it; the ownership rule stays.
Any polling agent may claim an open request; the claim shows which agent has it so others skip it.
The inbox shows all MCP agent activity (requests, replies, agent annotations, research comments, all agent writes), emphasizing the useful back-and-forth and de-ranking mundane updates.
First release surfaces: notes and tasks. Research cards and archived pages come later (research comments still appear in the inbox).

Inbox has two tiers: Needs you (agent replies, proposed edits, agent questions, new agent annotations) stays on top until acted on or dismissed; routine agent writes collapse to one line per agent run.
Agent marks a request ready for review; Byron closes it, or replies to reopen it.
Proposed edits show inline in the note as suggestions; Byron accepts or rejects per block or all at once.
Annotations have user-defined types. A type sets the color and a mark-for-AI flag. There is a default type, and the type can be changed when creating an annotation.
Agents may annotate at any time technically, but tool guidance tells them to annotate or update a note only when explicitly asked.
Agents can read annotations of every type as context, but act only on types flagged for AI.
On task requests the agent acts directly (subtasks, dates, linked note), then replies and marks the request ready.
Byron wants requests, annotations, proposals, and the inbox released together rather than as separate slices.

claims.statement: A live count badge on an Inbox sidebar link signals new Needs-you items. No digest or push.
No standing agent instructions in the app; the scheduled prompt of each agent says what to do.
Agent annotations use a built-in From AI type.
claims.notes: Provisional default; Byron did not choose between From AI and agent-picked types.

conflicts.note: 'Expand this content' needs a way to change the user's note without breaking the ownership rule.

human_questions.question: Should agents always annotate with a built-in From AI type, or pick from your types?

shape.appetite: One release with all four pieces (C22); internal order by risk.
shape.problem: Requests to polling agents have no home in the app, and agent responses are scattered across notes and the activity log.
shape.recommended_shape: One Annotation record family (note-level or passage-anchored by blockId+quote, typed, optional request status/claim, reply thread, optional edit proposal using notes_edit_blocks ops) on notes and tasks; annotation rail opposite TOC drawn as editor decorations; /inbox page with Needs you, Waiting on agents, and per-run agent activity from the MCP call log; sidebar badge; MCP tools inbox_get, inbox_claim, inbox_reply, notes_annotate, notes_propose_edits; research comments read in place.

success_moves.move: Accept proposals as an editor transaction, not a server write.
success_moves.risk: Second writer races autosave and deferred remote content (recent fixes #293).

success_moves.move: Anchor highlights by blockId + quoted text as decorations outside note content.
success_moves.risk: Marks in content would change text, revisions, search, export, and agent ownership rules.

success_moves.move: Reuse notes_edit_blocks op shape (replace, insert_after, delete) for proposals, with per-block base hashes for staleness.
success_moves.risk: A new edit grammar for agents and a conflict model from scratch.

success_moves.move: Leave ResearchComment in place; inbox and inbox_get read it.
success_moves.risk: Migration and research UI churn for no user-visible gain.

success_moves.move: Drive the first proof with a local fake agent (mcp-smoke style) and confirm a real ChatGPT scheduled task only afterwards.
success_moves.risk: Debugging through unattended ChatGPT runs with unclear write-approval behavior.

success_moves.move: Build the lower inbox tier from existing mcp.call ActionEvents grouped by requestId/agent.

first_proof.question: Can agent-proposed block edits render inline and be accepted in an open editor, through autosave, without fighting live or deferred content, while passage anchors survive nearby edits?
first_proof.artifact: Seeded local note + mcp-smoke style fake agent that claims, annotates, and proposes replace+insert; manual accept with typing in another block.
first_proof.decision_rule: If inline accept lands through autosave with no lost keystrokes and anchors hold, build on editor-side accept; otherwise fall back to an inbox diff with server-side accept-all and editor reload.

rabbit_holes.risk: Inline suggestion rendering inside TipTap NodeViews (code blocks, tables, task refs).
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Proposals target whole top-level blocks; unusual node types show as a plain before/after card.

rabbit_holes.risk: ChatGPT scheduled tasks may not auto-run write tools against custom connectors, or plan tiers may limit it.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Live smoke after local proof; any MCP client that polls still works.

rabbit_holes.risk: Anchor drift when the quoted passage is edited heavily.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Map decorations through edits and persist the updated quote on save; detach to passage removed.

open_decisions.question: Agent annotations: always From AI type, or agents may pick your types?
